Hand-authored author judgment, kept as a published script INPUT (the WS-X qualitative-ratings.json pattern) so that re-running scripts/probe_results.py can never silently overwrite a human verdict. Every verdict carries the one-line reason SC8 requires. No key in probes/questions-p*.md was edited at any point; scoring happened only after the last probe session ended (PROTOCOL section 1).

harness_deviations.D1_setting_sources: The driver runs with --setting-sources project, excluding the user and local sources. Every corpus repo carries a .claude/settings.local.json with "defaultMode": "bypassPermissions" and Read(//mnt/c/Users/olegr/PycharmProjects/**); loading it would have handed the subject every sibling repository and voided H1. No corpus repo has a .claude/settings.json (the project source), verified by inspection before run 1, so this excludes a permission escalation and nothing else. The project source is retained because it is what keeps in-tree CLAUDE.md auto-discovery working (H3) - verified in a pre-run mechanics test where --setting-sources "" suppressed CLAUDE.md loading entirely.
harness_deviations.D2_turn_caps_scored_not_enforced: Claude Code 2.1.220 exposes no --max-turns, so H6's caps (50 agentic turns for orientation, 15 per question) cannot halt a step mid-flight. Per-step turn counts are recorded for every step and H6's stated consequence is applied at scoring time: a question that exceeded the cap without an ANSWER line scores ABSTAINED with flag cap_hit. Questions that exceeded the cap but produced an ANSWER line are flagged over_cap and published rather than discarded.
harness_deviations.D3_repo_derived_context_in_F1: Claude Code injects a dynamic system-prompt section carrying the working directory, `git status`, and the most recent commit subjects. Every F1 response therefore includes repo-derived history the subject did not read itself. This is repo-carried substrate, inside what H1 already grants (read-only git), and identical in kind across all three projects, so it is accepted under H4 rather than treated as leakage - but it is disclosed here because H4's literal pass criterion is 'the working-directory name and content auto-loaded from in-tree files'. No F1 response in any session named a fact from outside its tree.

declared_protocol_extension.why_this_is_an_extension: PROTOCOL H9 provides for voiding a question whose receipt no longer holds against the repo - that is how P1-Q07 was voided. It does not contemplate the operator's recollection contradicting a key. This is therefore an extension, declared rather than smuggled in, and adopted under section 10's instruction that anything unanticipated is handled by voiding and reporting, never by improvising a new procedure or editing a key.
declared_protocol_extension.rule_adopted_at_review: Tier A / Tier B. Tier A is an artifact that STATES a decision in words (ADR, OQ resolution, doc sentence, commit body giving the choice and its reason). Tier B is a decision INFERRED from a diff, rename or config change that states nothing. Tier B may ground a claim about the STATE of the code; it may never ground a claim that 'we decided X' - not in a probe key, not in an exhibit, not in the talk.
declared_protocol_extension.direction_of_the_corrections: All three voids remove questions in the direction that HELPS the projects the hypothesis predicts should look worse: b-autobot loses both its confabulations, btest loses its only one, blive is unaffected.
